name: Xanthinuria Type I

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Xanthinuria Type I

criteria.description: Persistently low serum uric acid levels
Demonstrated deficiency of xanthine oxidase enzyme activity in biochemical assays
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the XDH gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of low serum uric acid, elevated urinary xanthine, and confirmed xanthine oxidase deficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic radiolucent stones due to xanthine accumulation
Markedly decreased serum uric acid levels

common.notes: Repeated kidney stone formation causing flank pain
Microscopic or gross blood in urine
Acute flank pain due to stone obstruction
Indicative of impaired renal function in some patients
searchTerms: mild to moderate high blood creatinine

occasional.symptomName: Muscle cramps secondary to renal impairment
occasional.notes: May occur due to electrolyte imbalance
searchTerms: muscle cramps caused by kidney problems
muscle pain related to kidney disease

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: fatigue linked to chronic kidney failure
low energy due to kidney problems

occasional.notes: Due to renal colic or stone passage

rare.symptomName: Xanthine crystal deposition in soft tissues
searchTerms: deposits of xanthine in body tissues
soft tissue buildup of xanthine crystals

rare.notes: Secondary hypertension due to renal impairment

laboratory: Markedly low serum uric acid concentration
Elevated urinary xanthine and hypoxanthine levels
Normal or low serum creatinine in early stages
imaging: Radiolucent kidney stones visible on ultrasound or CT
other: Reduced or absent xanthine oxidase enzyme activity in biochemical assays

distinguishingFeatures: Different genetic mutations in both XDH and AOX1 genes
Low serum uric acid without elevated urinary xanthine
Different genetic causes affecting urate transporters

redFlags: Severe hypouricemia with recurrent radiolucent kidney stones
Evidence of xanthine crystal deposition causing renal impairment
references: Ichida K, Amaya Y, Kamatani N, et al. Clinical and molecular analysis of xanthinuria in Japan. J Clin Invest. 1997;99(9):2391-2399.
Stiburkova B, Krijt J, Vyletal P, et al. Xanthinuria type I: a rare cause of urolithiasis. Clin Nephrol. 2012;77(3):243-248.
